active_product_bottleneck.observation: Actual Builder repeatedly preserves >9.33 MB Office savings with exactness/read-side economics, but safe snapshot control misses create law. Run 35931494298 measured base 134.960 ms, candidate 239.212 ms, proof 52.87 ms, staging 64.70 ms, commit/retention 20.74 ms. The frozen <=1.25x Office ceiling is 168.700 ms. Deleting proof alone leaves ~186.342 ms (~1.381x), so proof-only fusion cannot pass. Self-review found the stronger bound: deleting both measured proof and commit/retention leaves ~165.602 ms (~1.227x), inside the ceiling by only ~3.10 ms. Therefore a narrow path still exists if staging can become the single validation/construction pass and staged identities eliminate most commit rehash work; a deeper deflate-backed candidate is conditional, not yet proven necessary. The charged mode1-only oracle retains only 5,570,902 B median, so abandoning canonical mode0 still surrenders ~40.3% of the byte gain.

Measure how much of the 20.74 ms commit phase is actually removable. If enough survives to make proof+commit fusion plausibly <=1.25x, fuse ownership verification into the staging pass; otherwise escalate to the bounded deflate-backed candidate representation. Native mode0 projection remains earned debt.

process_lessons.lesson: continue-on-error step conclusion can mask underlying outcome; consume the final enforcement and artifact before declaring a gate green.
Deleting filesystem I/O is not equivalent to deleting work; measure phase internals after each intervention.
Never trade away a mutation/correctness boundary for a performance green.
A simpler already-supported representation must be fully charged before it can retire portability debt; mode1's read win did not compensate for surrendering ~40% of byte gain.

Use phase subtraction as an impossibility bound, but subtract combinations as well as individual phases before declaring a representation change mandatory; proof alone cannot close this gate, while proof+commit still has a narrow measured path.
